cover.headline: A record quarter on a war-time phenol spike, a ₹8,600 cr capex bill ahead: the price assumes too much
cover.lead: Deepak Nitrite makes phenol, acetone and IPA (Phenolics, ~70% of revenue) and nitration-based chemical intermediates (Advanced Intermediates, ~30%). Q1FY27 was its best quarter ever (net profit ₹345 cr, +207%) because the Middle East war widened phenol spreads. We think that spike fades: spreads were already easing in August, and a new 345 ktpa domestic phenol plant (Haldia Petrochemicals) is due to start in October 2026. Meanwhile ~₹8,600 cr of capex over FY27-29 for a propylene-to-polycarbonate chain adds depreciation, interest and debt well before it adds revenue. We value Deepak Nitrite the way the street does, on **P/E: 25x Sep-28E EPS of ₹45.5**. That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** EV/EBITDA (₹1,093) confirms it; our DCF (₹202) says today's cash flows support far less. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Q1 was a spike, not a new base
arguments.p: Phenolics EBIT jumped to ₹418 cr (23.5% margin) in Q1FY27 from ₹118 cr a year earlier, on war-time spreads (PL: "amid supply disruptions caused by the West Asia crisis"). Phenolics margins have swung from 28% (FY21) to ~14% (FY23-26) with the global cycle. PL notes spreads were already moderating week by week in August, and Haldia's 345 ktpa plant (close to Deepak's own ~350-400 ktpa) is due within weeks. We model Phenolics EBITDA margin 17.5% in FY27 and 14% after.

arguments.h: Advanced Intermediates: new plants, old problem
arguments.p: AI EBIT fell from ₹596 cr (FY22) to ₹107 cr (FY26) as Chinese pricing hit; the segment earned a 4.8% pre-tax return on capital in FY26 after ₹1,004 cr of new plants. Q1FY27 recovered to an 8.3% EBIT margin. China's curbs on nitration help, but the new nitric acid plant ran at ~45% in Q4FY26 and two plants slipped. We assume margins recover to 15.5% EBITDA by FY29, still well below FY22-24.

arguments.h: The polycarbonate bet: big, late and debt-funded
arguments.p: The ₹11,500 cr propylene-to-polycarbonate programme (plus a ₹2,500 cr BPA plant approved in August) is the long-term story. But the start date has slipped twice (Dec-2027 → Jun-2028 → H2 FY28-29), its returns are undisclosed and global PC capacity is growing. Net debt rises from ₹1,156 cr to ~₹7,500 cr by FY29 in our model; ROE falls to ~8%, below the 12.5% cost of equity.

arguments.h: Valuation: the street's own yardstick says too expensive
arguments.p: Brokers use 24-29x FY28E EPS. Our FY28E EPS (₹47.1) is 14% below PL and 25% below Motilal Oswal because we assume normal spreads and charge the project's depreciation and interest. At ₹1,530 the stock trades at 32.5x our FY28E; our 25x (the ~36x one-year-forward median since 2021, cut by the sector's ~30% de-rating) gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due Oct/Nov-2026): how far Phenolics margins fall after the war-time peak; first MIBK/MIBC sales.
Start-up of Haldia Petrochemicals' 345 ktpa phenol plant (due to start in October 2026) and its effect on Indian phenol prices.
Commissioning of the multipurpose agro-intermediates and alkylation plants (commercial volumes from January 2027) and stable running of the nitric acid plant.
Polycarbonate milestones: relocation of the Stade (Germany) equipment, civil works, any further slip beyond H2 FY28-29; firm cost of the BPA plant.
Funding: drawdown of the tied-up project debt; any equity raise (management: "if at all required, we'll approach the market").

sections.title: Two businesses: a phenol commodity plant and a nitration chemistry house

blocks.p: Deepak Nitrite was founded in 1970 to make sodium nitrite. It grew into a maker of chemical intermediates (nitro-toluidines, xylidines, oximes, optical brighteners) for dyes, agrochemicals, pharma and rubber, and in FY19-20 its subsidiary Deepak Phenolics started a world-scale cumene-phenol-acetone complex at Dahej. Phenolics now brings ~70% of revenue and ~85% of segment profit. A second subsidiary, Deepak Chem Tech (DCTL), is the growth vehicle: nitric acid, nitration, hydrogenation, fluorination, MIBK/MIBC and the polycarbonate programme. Seven plants at five locations, 36+ products, 1,500+ customers; 85% of Q1FY27 revenue was domestic.

blocks.p: **Phenolics is a spread business.** Benzene and propylene make cumene, which splits into phenol and acetone (roughly 1 tonne of phenol gives ~0.6 tonne of acetone); acetone is also turned into IPA, and from FY27 into MIBK/MIBC. Profit depends on the gap between product prices and feedstock costs (the "spread"), which is set by global supply: Indian prices track import parity. Deepak's edge is scale, logistics and reliability for thousands of Indian buyers (laminates, plywood, pharma, agrochemicals) who prefer not to import. **Advanced Intermediates is a chemistry business**: nitration, reduction and diazotization of aromatics, sold to dye, agro and pharma makers worldwide. It competes head-on with Chinese producers, which is why its margins collapsed in FY24-26.

blocks.callout: **Corporate actions:** No bonus, split, buyback, QIP or rights issue found in the FY20-FY27 filings reviewed; equity unchanged at 13.64 cr shares of ₹2. sections.title: Phenol is a global commodity; India is short, but not for long

blocks.p: India consumes more phenol and acetone than it makes, so Deepak Phenolics sells at import parity and earns whatever the Asian spread allows. In FY26 Chinese and Korean additions "caused margins to collapse in the Asian market" (DPL's chairman). Then the Middle East war disrupted feedstock and freight in Q4FY26-Q1FY27; India even waived import duty on phenol from 2-Apr to 30-Jun-2026, yet spreads widened sharply "amid supply disruptions caused by the West Asia crisis" (PL), and domestic suppliers earned record margins. Two things now work against Deepak: global capacity remains ample, and **Haldia Petrochemicals' ₹6,000 cr phenol-acetone complex (345 ktpa phenol, close to Deepak's own capacity) was due to start in October 2026.** In the August call the Group CFO said "no new capacities are coming up". We disagree.

sections.title: Phenolics: a well-run plant, priced by the world, with a new rival next door

pair.title: Phenolics EBIT: ₹418 cr in Q1FY27

bullets: **Volumes are not the issue.** DPL runs at ~165% of the plant's original capacity after ₹80-100 cr of debottlenecking, hit record production in FY26 and is spending ~₹70 cr more to approach 400 ktpa of phenol. Management will not disclose volumes or spreads.

**Margins are the issue.** Segment EBITDA margin: 12.5% (FY20), 28.1% (FY21), 22.6% (FY22), 13.8-14.9% (FY23-26). Excluding the Gujarat GST incentive (₹161 cr in FY25, ₹102 cr in FY26), FY25-26 margins were only 12.1% and 12.7%. Q1FY27's 23.5% EBIT margin (22.6% excluding a ₹21.5 cr incentive) came from war-time spreads.

**Downstream additions** (MIBK, MIBC, acetophenone, commissioning from August 2026) add value to acetone. Management says pre-commissioning met design norms and MIBC exceeded design capacity, but declined to quantify revenue. China is oversupplied in MIBK (Feb-2026 call).
**Competition**: Haldia's 345 ktpa plant targets the same Indian buyers from Q3FY27. Deepak's answer is reliability and just-in-time supply ("Depend on Deepak"); that protects volume, not price.

pair.title: Without the state incentive, margins were ~12-13%

pair.title: Our Phenolics forecast: margin back to ~14%

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Phenolics is a good asset with high returns on depreciated capital (pre-tax ROCE 36.4% in FY26), but it has no pricing power. We model revenue +17% in FY27 (Q1 plus ~₹1,500 cr a quarter), +2% in FY28 as prices normalise against more volume and MIBK/MIBC, and +10% in FY29; EBITDA margin 17.5% then 14%, i.e. mid-cycle including the incentive.

bullets: **What went wrong.** Chinese oversupply in nitration chemistries cut prices: AI revenue fell from ₹3,034 cr (FY23) to ~₹2,400 cr a year, "a substantial amount… because of pricing" (Feb-2026). Management chose to push volume into the market ahead of its new nitric acid plant "even if it comes at a short-term impact on price".

**New plants.** DCTL commissioned hydrogenation-I (Sep-2025, ₹115 cr), nitration + hydrogenation-II (Jan-2026, ₹85 cr) and a ₹515 cr nitric acid plant (Dec-2025), completing "ammonia-to-amines" integration. Nitric acid is captive (no external revenue); it ran at ~45% in Q4FY26 on technical problems, forcing purchases at high prices. These plants pushed FY26 AI capex to ₹1,004 cr and segment capital employed to ₹2,215 cr.

**What should improve.** China's curbs on hazardous chemistries; lower US duty on sodium nitrite; multipurpose agro-intermediates and alkylation plants (commercial volumes from January 2027); fluorination and photochlorination products. Management: new products are "in line or better" than AI's average margin, but it will not size them.

sections.title: The polycarbonate programme: India's first, but late, large and debt-funded

blocks.p: DCTL is building an integrated chain at Dahej: propylene and benzene → cumene → phenol and acetone → bisphenol-A (BPA) → polycarbonate (PC) resin → compounds. It bought Trinseo's 165,000 tpa PC plant at Stade, Germany (with technology and the CALIBRE™ brand), which is being dismantled and shipped to India. India imports more than 300,000 tonnes of PC resin a year and has no local maker. The programme is costed at ₹11,500 cr, funded 60:40 debt to equity with all debt tied up; a ₹2,500 cr BPA plant (up to 240 ktpa) was approved on 4-Aug-2026, and it is not confirmed whether that is inside the ₹11,500 cr.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the project is strategically logical (import substitution, integration into its own phenol) and could transform the company in the 2030s. But (1) its returns are undisclosed; (2) global PC capacity is growing (PL downgraded the stock for this reason in April); (3) the start has slipped twice; (4) depreciation and interest arrive before revenue. In our model net debt reaches ~₹7,500 cr at Mar-29 and EPS falls in FY28-29. We include no meaningful PC profit before FY30, so PC upside is the main thing a buyer at today's price is paying for.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard
blocks.source: GAM research compilation (company filings and calls to Sep-2026)

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Deepak has a **scale and service advantage**, not a moat in the pricing sense. In phenol it is the biggest local supplier to thousands of small buyers who value reliable, just-in-time supply; that protects volume. But the price is set by global spreads, and a second domestic producer arrives in Q3FY27. In intermediates its know-how is real, yet Chinese pricing took AI margins from 27% to 9% in four years. A business like this earns high returns at the top of the cycle (ROE 46% in FY20, 38% in FY22) and below its cost of capital at the bottom; it does not compound steadily.

sections.title: A phenol boom, four years of falling profits, and a record quarter

blocks.p: Deepak Nitrite's revenue rose from ₹1,651 cr in FY18 to ₹6,802 cr in FY22 as the Dahej phenol complex came on stream and the Covid-era phenol shortage lifted prices. Net profit peaked at ₹1,067 cr (EPS ₹78) in FY22. Then it fell for four straight years, to ₹551 cr (EPS ₹40) in FY26, while revenue stayed flat at ₹7,700-8,300 cr: Chinese capacity pushed down phenol spreads and the prices of its nitration chemicals. Q1FY27 broke the trend: revenue +36%, net profit ₹345 cr (+207%), the best quarter ever, as the Middle East war widened phenol spreads.

pair.title: Revenue: flat for four years after the FY19-22 jump
Net profit has halved since FY22
EBITDA margin: 29% at the peak, 12.5% in FY26
Quarterly profit: Q1FY27 is three times a normal quarter

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a cyclical business. Profit follows the phenol spread and the price of Chinese intermediates, not a steady growth line. FY21-22 earnings were a boom; FY25-26 were close to a trough; Q1FY27 is another spike. Neither extreme is a good base for valuation, which is why we value the stock on Sep-28E earnings after spreads normalise.

sections.title: Ten years of capex ate all the cash, and returns have fallen from 44% to 11%

blocks.p: Over FY17-26 Deepak Nitrite generated ₹5,571 cr of operating cash and spent ₹5,457 cr on plants: 98 paise of every rupee. The first half of that money (FY17-21, mainly the Dahej phenol complex) earned superbly: ROCE reached 40-44% in FY21-22. The second half (FY22-26) went into nitric acid, nitration, hydrogenation and fluorination plants, and into the start of the polycarbonate project. So far it has earned little: ROCE fell to 11% in FY26, below any reasonable cost of capital, and the AI segment's own pre-tax ROCE was under 5%.

pair.title: Capex vs operating cash flow
ROCE: from 44% (FY22) to 11% (FY26)

blocks.callout: **The bigger bill is still to come.** FY27-29 capex is guided and modelled at ~₹8,600 cr, 1.6x the previous ten years combined, for the ₹11,500 cr propylene-to-polycarbonate programme, a ₹2,500 cr BPA plant and smaller projects. Polycarbonate is not expected to start before H2 FY28-29. Until then shareholders carry the debt, interest and depreciation without the revenue.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but state incentives and timing items to strip out

bullets: **Gujarat GST incentive inside revenue.** Deepak Phenolics books a state incentive (scheme "Incentive to Industries (General) 2016-2021") as revenue: ₹161 cr in FY25 (all in Q4), ₹102 cr in FY26 (₹68 cr in Q4) and ₹21.5 cr in Q1FY27. That was ~15% of FY26 Phenolics EBIT. Its remaining life is not disclosed; a lumpy Q4 booking flatters the March quarter.

**Feedstock timing.** In May management said it had bought benzene, toluene and xylene "at every dip" and held "a much larger inventory" at "enviable prices" into mid-Q2FY27; in August it said there was no inventory benefit in Q1. Both cannot be fully true; we assume some of Q1's margin was timing.
**Capitalised interest.** Borrowing costs on the PC project are capitalised until commissioning (Ind AS 23), so P&L interest understates the true cost of the debt in FY27-28 and jumps after start-up.
**Ramp-up losses in DCTL** depressed AI EBIT in FY26 (company disclosure) and the nitric acid plant ran at ~45%; FY26 also had a ₹12.8 cr Labour Code exceptional charge.
**Definitions.** The company's EBITDA includes other income (FY26: ₹1,041 cr); Screener's and ours exclude it (₹987 cr).
**Audit.** Deloitte Haskins & Sells: clean opinion, no key audit matters, audit trail operated throughout FY26. Contingent liabilities negligible (₹0.5 cr).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The books are clean and the auditor is a Big-4 firm. But reported Phenolics profit includes a state incentive worth ₹100-160 cr a year with no disclosed end-date, management's messages on inventory gains conflict, and capitalised interest will flatter FY27-28 profit. Investors should look at margins excluding the incentive.

sections.title: From net cash to ~₹7,500 cr of net debt in three years

blocks.p: Deepak Nitrite had net cash in FY22-24. Borrowings rose from ₹286 cr (Mar-24) to ₹1,638 cr (Mar-26) as DCTL spent on new plants, and net debt reached ₹1,156 cr, about 1.2x FY26 EBITDA. The polycarbonate debt is fully tied up (60:40 debt to equity); management expects peak borrowing of ₹8,000-8,500 cr including working capital and says debt will stay below equity. Our model has net debt of ~₹3,000 cr at Mar-27 and ~₹7,500 cr at Mar-29 (~5x FY29E EBITDA). Working capital is the other strain: receivable days rose from 56 to 70 in FY26 as the company moved some customers to a dealer/consignment model.

sections.title: Ownership: a Mehta family company held mainly by Indian institutions

blocks.p: The Mehta family (Chairman Deepak C. Mehta and his son, CEO Maulik Mehta) and family investment companies own 49.34% (Jun-2026), with no pledge reported. Indian institutions own 23.76%, led by LIC (9.5%); foreign investors only 6.24%. The number of shareholders fell from 4.51 lakh to 3.83 lakh in two years as retail investors left after the fall from the Aug-2024 peak.

sections.title: Our forecasts: in line for FY27, well below the street for FY28

blocks.p: We forecast each segment's revenue and EBITDA margin (segment EBIT plus its depreciation), remove inter-segment sales, and deduct central costs. Capex follows guidance (~₹2,500 cr in FY27, ~₹3,300 cr in FY28, ~₹2,800 cr in FY29), so depreciation and interest rise ahead of polycarbonate revenue. Every assumption, with our reasoning, is in the Excel model's Assumptions sheet, which recalculates this report's target price.

FY29 EPS dips again as polycarbonate depreciation and interest start before its revenue: that is the J-curve of the project.

sections.title: The street: mostly negative already; we are more negative still

blocks.p: Latest call per broker by 30-Sep-2026: 1 Buy (Emkay ₹2,000), 1 Reduce (PL ₹1,586), 2 Sell (MOSL ₹1,500, HDFC Securities ₹1,327). Kotak's rating is suspended. Both brokers with a disclosed method use P/E on FY28E EPS (24-29x). Bulls (Emkay) point to the AI recovery, favourable spreads and phenol-2 revenue from FY29. Bears point to normalising spreads, global phenol and polycarbonate overcapacity, and rising leverage. Our target is the lowest because our FY28E earnings are lower (we assume spreads normalise and charge the project costs) and because we apply a de-rated multiple.

blocks.callout: **What the cross-checks tell us.** EV/EBITDA at 15x Sep-28E (the ~23x five-year median less the same de-rating) lands 4% below the P/E target: it charges the project debt explicitly. The DCF is far lower (₹202): even with polycarbonate lifting revenue ~14% a year to FY31 and the margin to 18%, the ~₹8,600 cr of FY27-29 capex earns less than a 12.5% cost of equity. In other words, today's price already assumes polycarbonate returns well above anything management has disclosed.

cells: Phenolics revenue +17% / +2% / +10% (FY27-29E) at 17.5% then 14% EBITDA margin; AI +18% / +12% / +10% at 12.5-15.5%; 25x Sep-28E EPS.

blocks.p: The engine fades capex in a straight line from the last forecast year. With the usual 15-year horizon that would keep capex at 15-25% of revenue for a decade and give a negative value, which is meaningless. We therefore use a two-stage DCF: explicit FY28-29, a transition year (FY30) with BPA and phenol-2 spend still running, a steady state from FY31 (18% EBITDA margin, capex 5% of revenue, revenue up ~14% as polycarbonate ramps), then 6% growth for ever. The engine discounts at the cost of equity (12.5%), which is harsh for a company funding ~60% of its project with debt; the sensitivity table shows lower discount rates.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good operator at the top of a spread cycle, priced for a project not yet built

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest phenol and acetone producer (a well-run, high-return plant with no pricing power), a nitration intermediates business still recovering from Chinese competition, and a large option on India's first integrated polycarbonate chain, funded with debt and due in H2 FY28-29.

**What you are paying:** 32.5x our FY28E EPS and 33.6x Sep-28E, against 24-29x that even the brokers use on higher earnings. On the street's own method and our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). Q1FY27's record profit came from a war-time spread that is already fading, while ₹8,600 cr of capex adds costs before revenue.

**Biggest swing factor:** the phenol-acetone spread. Every one-point change in the Phenolics EBITDA margin moves FY28E EPS by ~₹3.5 (≈7%).
**Second swing factor:** the polycarbonate project's timing and returns, which the market is pricing ahead of any disclosure.

Glossary

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: Two basic chemicals made together from cumene. Phenol goes into resins (laminates, plywood), pharma, agrochemicals and bisphenol-A; acetone into solvents, IPA, MIBK and BPA.
Made from benzene and propylene; split into phenol and acetone.
Isopropyl alcohol: a solvent and disinfectant, made by Deepak from acetone.
Methyl isobutyl ketone / carbinol: solvents made from acetone; India imports them.
Bisphenol-A: made from phenol and acetone; the main raw material for polycarbonate.
A tough, clear engineering plastic used in cars, electronics, construction and medical devices.
The gap between the selling price of a product and the cost of its feedstock; the main driver of Phenolics profit.
Chemical reactions Deepak specialises in: adding a nitro group, adding hydrogen (making amines), and turning amines into reactive intermediates (e.g. for fluorination).
Sodium nitrite, xylidines, oximes, OBA, DASDA
Advanced Intermediates products used in dyes, agrochemicals, rubber, paper and detergents (OBA = optical brightening agent; DASDA is its key intermediate).
Propane dehydrogenation: makes propylene from propane (Petronet LNG will supply Deepak's phenol-2 by pipeline).
Capital work in progress: money spent on plants not yet running; not depreciated until commissioned.
Interest on loans for a plant under construction, added to the plant's cost instead of the P&L until it starts.
Operating profit of a business before (EBIT) or before and after adding back (EBITDA) its depreciation, excluding head-office costs and other income.
Share price ÷ earnings per share; enterprise value (market value + net debt) ÷ EBITDA.
Discounted cash flow valuation; Ke is the cost of equity (here 12.5% = 6.5% risk-free + 1.0 × 6% equity risk premium).
Return on capital employed / on shareholders' equity.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Deepak Nitrite (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven: Advanced Intermediates and Phenolics each grow revenue and earn an EBITDA margin (segment EBIT + segment depreciation). A third line removes inter-segment sales. Group EBITDA = sum of segments less central costs (Screener basis, excluding other income). Valued on P/E, as the street does.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates
segments._why: FY27: Q1 +33% (better prices after the Middle East war, recovery in nitrites and fuel additives, new nitration/hydrogenation output); Q2-Q4 assumed +12% as war-time prices fade, with the multipurpose agro-intermediates and alkylation plants adding volume only from January 2027. FY28 +12%: first full year of the new DCTL plants and fluorination products. FY29 +10%. AI revenue was ₹3,034 cr in FY23; we reach ₹3,700 cr only in FY29.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 26.6% (FY22), 20.8% (FY23), 19.6% (FY24), 11.4% (FY25), 9.3% (FY26). Q1FY27 EBIT margin 8.3% (~13% EBITDA). Captive nitric acid (once it runs reliably), China's curbs on nitration and new products should lift margins, but Chinese pricing still sets the ceiling: 12.5% / 14.5% / 15.5%, well below the FY22-24 levels.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments._why: FY27: Q1 ₹1,775 cr (+36%) on war-time spreads (West Asia supply disruptions); we assume ~₹1,500 cr a quarter for Q2-Q4 as prices normalise and Haldia Petrochemicals' new 345 ktpa phenol plant (due to start in October 2026) starts selling: +17%. FY28 +2%: lower phenol/acetone prices offset by ~10% more volume (debottlenecking to ~400 ktpa) and the first full year of MIBK/MIBC and acetophenone. FY29 +10%: volume growth plus a small start to polycarbonate (commissioning targeted H2 FY28-29).
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 12.5% (FY20), 28.1% (FY21), 22.6% (FY22), 13.8-14.9% (FY23-26, including a Gujarat GST incentive worth ~1.9-2.8 points in FY25-26). Q1FY27 ~25% (EBIT 23.5%). We assume ~25% in Q1, ~19% in Q2 and ~12% in H2 (FY27: 17.5%), then 14% (mid-cycle, incentive included) as a new domestic competitor and Chinese capacity cap spreads.

segments.name: Inter-segment eliminations
segments._why: Sales between the segments, removed on consolidation: ₹50 cr (FY25), ₹67 cr (FY26), only ₹1 cr in Q1FY27. We assume ~₹40 cr in FY27, growing 10% a year.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Central costs not allocated to segments (reported EBITDA below the sum of segment EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA (which excludes other income): ₹34 cr (FY22), ₹24 cr (FY23), ₹58 cr (FY25), ₹39 cr (FY26); FY24 ₹128 cr includes items Screener moved to other income. We assume ₹45-55 cr as head office grows with DCTL.
assumptions._capexWhy: Guidance ~₹2,500 cr for FY27 (Feb-2026), of which ₹1,500-1,600 cr for the polycarbonate programme (Aug-2026); ~₹3,000 cr on polycarbonate in 2027-28 plus debottlenecking and maintenance; FY29 completes PC and starts BPA (₹2,500 cr approved Aug-2026). Total FY27-29 ₹8,600 cr; FY26 actual ₹1,199 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹225 cr = 5.5% of average gross block. The engine depreciates all capex at once, but most of the FY27-29 spend sits in capital work in progress until polycarbonate starts (H2 FY28-29). 4.3% gives ~₹250 cr / ~₹380 cr / ~₹510 cr: slightly low for FY27 (Q1 run-rate ₹64 cr a quarter plus new plants), slightly high for FY28, and FY29 includes part-year PC depreciation.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt, so no treasury income; other income entered separately.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Other income ₹45 cr in FY26 (normal, Screener), ₹14 cr in Q1FY27; cash balances fall as capex is funded.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹46 cr; Q1FY27 ₹23 cr. Borrowings rise to ~₹7,500 cr by FY29 (management: peak ₹8,000-8,500 cr), but interest on the PC loans is capitalised until commissioning (Ind AS 23). FY29 includes part-year interest on the PC debt after start-up.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective 27.3% (incl. CSR and other disallowances); Q1FY27 26.2%; statutory 25.17%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: ₹7.5 a share for four years (FY26 payout 19%); we assume the dividend stays near ₹7-8 while capex is heavy.

dcf._betaWhy: Commodity-linked chemicals with a large project under way: market-like risk.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian demand for phenol, acetone and polycarbonate tracks industrial growth; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth of ~12% in FY30 and 14% in FY31 as polycarbonate (165 ktpa, ~₹4,000 cr of revenue at full rates) ramps up; then 6% for ever.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: An integrated propylene-to-polycarbonate chain should earn more than merchant phenol: 18% steady-state EBITDA margin (FY23-26 group average ~14%; FY21-22 peak 24-29%).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~26% of revenue in FY29 to 5% (maintenance plus debottlenecking) by FY31, once PC/BPA are built.
dcf._yearsWhy: Two-stage DCF: explicit FY28-29 (peak capex), FY30 a transition year (half-way to steady state, with BPA/phenol-2 spend still running), steady state from FY31, then a terminal value at 6% growth. The engine fades capex in a straight line from the last forecast year; with the house 15-year horizon that keeps capex at 15-25% of revenue for a decade and the DCF turns negative. A short horizon is the only way to let capex fall back to maintenance levels once the project is finished.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Spreads stay firm as Chinese and European capacity closes and Haldia's new plant mostly replaces imports; AI margins return towards 18% as China curbs nitration and new products ramp; polycarbonate starts on time.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Phenol spreads fall back to the FY25-26 trough as Haldia's 345 ktpa plant and Chinese capacity flood the market; AI stays stuck near FY26 margins; polycarbonate slips again while debt and interest keep rising.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Deepak Nitrite: Motilal Oswal 24x and Prabhudas Lilladher 29x FY28E EPS (Aug-2026). 25x = the stock's ~36x one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 cut by the ~30% de-rating of Indian chemical stocks at 30-Sep-2026. Bull 32x (half the de-rating reverses), bear 20x (the 2020 level, before the phenol boom was priced in).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Charges the polycarbonate debt explicitly. 15x ≈ the ~23x five-year median EV/EBITDA less the same ~30% sector de-rating; peers at 30-Sep-2026: Aarti 16.0x, Vinati 16.9x, Atul 12.5x, SRF 19.8x trailing.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: explicit FY28-29, transition FY30, steady state FY31 (18% EBITDA margin, capex 5% of revenue), Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 6%, net debt deducted. It shows how much of the price depends on returns not yet visible.
